subject: Linguistics
title: Style-Shifting and Register
description: A quick, practical guide to Style-Shifting and Register.

hook.text: A professor might say 'gonna' in the pub and 'going to' in a lecture—same person, different register.

buildup.text: Register is the level of formality a speaker adopts—from casual to frozen formal.

discovery.text: Joos identified five registers: intimate, casual, consultative, formal, and frozen.

twist.text: Style-shifting is usually unconscious—speakers read the social situation and adjust automatically.

climax.text: Using the wrong register is a social misstep—too casual in court or too formal with friends.

punchline.text: Your words dress for the occasion—just like you do.

quiz.question: What is style-shifting?
options: Adjusting formality to match the social context
